concerns.text: Task T022a defines the 'dominant eigenvalue' as a 'single global scalar constant' derived from the whole dataset. This violates Constitution Principle VI and Spec FR-002, which mandate computing the covariance matrix and entanglement score 'for every sample'. A global constant cannot serve as a per-sample predictor in the Random Forest model (FR-004), effectively nullifying the core hypothesis test.

Task T022b calculates per-sample variance/entropy but omits the per-sample dominant eigenvalue required by Spec FR-002 and Constitution Principle VI. By splitting the eigenvalue calculation into a global constant (T022a) and per-sample stats (T022b), the task list fails to deliver the 'entanglement score' (defined as including eigenvalue) for each sample, weakening the feature set required for FR-004.

Task T037 mandates raising a RuntimeError if the Z-Reward dataset fetch fails with 'NO synthetic fallbacks'. While this aligns with Reproducibility, the Spec Assumptions state the dataset 'is available... or a specified archive'. If the public repo is down but an archive exists, this task blocks execution without a mechanism to use the alternative source, violating the 'feasibility' constraint of the plan and potentially halting the project on transient network issues.

Task T033 ('Code cleanup and refactoring') is marked 'FAILED: unspecified' and lacks a concrete acceptance criterion (e.g., 'ruff check passes with zero errors'). This makes the task untestable and its completion ambiguous, violating the requirement for verifiable deliverables in the task list.
